labels.label: prop:ring_both_continuous_extends

hypotheses.paper: A a Z/2Z-ring (l.52: noetherian, A/2A ≅ Z/2Z)
hypotheses.note: IsZ2Ring A, which includes IsDomain: the integral reading of OQ-42 (a). It is load-bearing. Integrality cancels powers of 2 in Z/2^nZ ≅ A/2^nA (Syracuse.two_pow_dvd_natCast_iff), in Krull (Syracuse.toZ2_injective), and in the uniqueness of halves and of the odd part of 3x+1 (Syracuse.f_map, T_map, continuous_f, continuousAt_T). Without it the l.52 claim fails even with 2 ≠ 0: ZMod 4 (Syracuse.zmod4_witness).

Added to every statement about A_2 or ι : A → Z_2 (OQ-42 (b)). For A = Z/2Z the completion is not Z_2 (Finding 3), and no ring hom Z/2Z → Z_2 exists. Not needed for the continuity of f_A and T_A on A: Syracuse.continuous_f and continuousAt_T hold in every Z/2Z-ring, Z/2Z included.

hypotheses.paper: the topology of 'the associated absolute value' |x| = 2^{-ν_2(x)} (l.52)
hypotheses.note: Any topology on A with IsAdic (Ideal.span {2}). Its neighbourhood basis at x is {y | 2^n ∣ y − x}, the closed balls of |·| (Syracuse.hasBasis_nhds_two). The hypothesis is satisfiable: Syracuse.isAdic_withIdeal gives the canonical instance. ι is an isometry for |·| (Syracuse.norm_toZ2).

A reading. A_2 = UniformSpace.Completion A, for any uniform ring structure on A whose topology is 2-adic. Its entourages are {(x,y) | x − y ∈ 2^nA}, the uniformity of |·|. Every statement is also given in Z_2 through ι (the _padicInt / _toZ2 forms), justified by Syracuse.completion_ringEquiv. The algebraic lim A/2^nA (AdicCompletion) is not formalized.

hypotheses.paper: f_A (l.55, its two cases printed swapped)
hypotheses.note: A reading: Syracuse.f halves the even elements and sends the odd ones to 3x+1 (OQ-42 (c), T-syr-base). The printed f_A does not exist (Syracuse.printed_f_not_definable).

Where the paper's T_A is meant, the condition 3x+1 ≠ 0 is added (OQ-42 (d)). Syracuse.T is total, with the junk value 0 at −1/3 when 2 ≠ 0 (Syracuse.T_of_three_mul_add_one_eq_zero). The extension statements are proved off −1/3, and refuted at −1/3.

hypotheses.paper: 'T_A … extends continuously to A_2 … their extension is T_{A_2}'
hypotheses.note: False as printed (Finding 1). Proved on A_2 ∖ {−1/3}: T_{A_2} is continuous there and extends T_A. It is the only continuous extension of T_A : 2A+1 → 2A+1 to (2A_2+1) ∖ {−1/3} (Syracuse.eqOn_T_completion_of_continuousOn_odd).

findings: syracuse.tex:58 — 'T_A … extends continuously to A_2' is false. Take A = Z, where T_Z is the paper's map on all of 2Z+1 (3x+1 ≠ 0 always). No g : Z_2 → Z_2 is continuous on 2Z_2+1 and agrees with T_Z on the odd integers (Syracuse.T_int_not_extends). The printed statement, quantified over all Z/2Z-rings with 2 ≠ 0, is refuted (Syracuse.printed_T_extends_false). In every Z/2Z-ring A with 2 ≠ 0, no extension of T_A to A_2 is continuous at −1/3 ∈ 2A_2+1 within 2A_2+1 (Syracuse.not_continuousWithinAt_extension_T, not_exists_continuousWithinAt_extension_T, not_exists_continuousWithinAt_extension_T_completion). The reason: the odd part of 3x+1 has no limit as x → −1/3. The integers c_j = (4^{j+1} − 1)/3 tend 2-adically to −1/3 with T(c_j) = 1, and d_j = (10·4^{j+1} − 1)/3 tend to −1/3 with T(d_j) = 5. Hence 'their extension is T_{A_2}' fails too: T_{A_2} is undefined at −1/3 (OQ-42 (d)), and no value there makes it continuous on 2A_2+1 (Syracuse.not_continuousWithinAt_T_padicInt for the junk value). Strongest true form (Syracuse.ring_both_continuous_extends): T_{A_2} is continuous on A_2 ∖ {−1/3}, extends T_A, and is the unique continuous extension of T_A : 2A+1 → 2A+1 to (2A_2+1) ∖ {−1/3}. This is the topological face of OQ-42 (d).

syracuse.tex:58 — 'T_A is continuous' holds wherever T_A is defined. T is continuous at every x with 3x+1 ≠ 0, in every Z/2Z-ring, Z/2Z included (Syracuse.continuousAt_T, continuousOn_T). For y − x ∈ 2^{n+k+1}A with k = ν_2(3x+1), one has T y − T x = 3(y − x)/2^k ∈ 2^{n+1}A. When 3 ∉ A^×, as in Z, T is continuous on all of A, hence on 2A+1 as printed (Syracuse.continuous_T_of_not_isUnit_three). When 3 ∈ A^×, as in Z_2, the printed T_A does not exist at −1/3.

syracuse.tex:52 — 'for any Z/2Z-ring A, A_2 is naturally isomorphic to Z_2' is false for A = Z/2Z. Its completion has 2 = 0 for every uniform ring structure, so it is not isomorphic to Z_2 (Syracuse.completion_zmod2_not_padicInt; for the 2-adic structure, completion_zmod2_twoAdic_not_padicInt). It holds for every other Z/2Z-ring, i.e. whenever 2 ≠ 0 (Syracuse.completion_ringEquiv, completion_twoAdic). The proof: every x is an integer modulo 2^nA, so Z/2^nZ ≅ A/2^nA (Syracuse.zmodEquivQuotient). The limit is a ring hom ι : A → Z_2 (Syracuse.toZ2). It is injective by Krull, preserves ν_2 and |·|, has dense image, and induces the 2-adic topology, so (Z_2, ι) is a completion of A (Syracuse.completionPkg). The resulting A_2 ≅ Z_2 is a ring isomorphism and a uniform isomorphism extending ι. 'Naturally' is proved in two ways: ι is the only ring hom A → Z_2 (Syracuse.toZ2_unique, toZ2_comp), and the isomorphism is the only ring isomorphism A_2 ≅ Z_2 (Syracuse.ringEquiv_padicInt_unique). The paper prints no proof ('one can show').

syracuse.tex:50–52 (evidence for OQ-42 (a)) — under the printed definition of l.52 (noetherian, A/2A ≅ Z/2Z, no integrality), the l.52 claim fails even with 2 ≠ 0. ZMod 4 is noetherian, has A/2A ≅ Z/2Z and 2 ≠ 0, and is not a domain. Its completion has 4 = 0 for every uniform ring structure, so it is not Z_2 (Syracuse.zmod4_witness). Integrality, which l.50 states but l.52 omits, is therefore load-bearing.

syracuse.tex:58 — the f_A half holds in the halve-the-even reading of OQ-42 (c) (the printed f_A does not exist, T-syr-base). f_A is continuous in every Z/2Z-ring (Syracuse.continuous_f). For 2 ≠ 0, f_{A_2} is continuous, extends f_A, and is its only continuous extension (Syracuse.continuous_f_completion, f_coe_completion, eq_f_completion_of_continuous; in Z_2 the same via ι: continuous_f_padicInt, f_toZ2, eq_f_of_continuous). The proof is left to the reader (l.57); none is printed.
questions: OQ-42 (d), topological face: which corrected form of 'T_A extends continuously to A_2' does the author intend? No continuous extension exists at −1/3. Reading taken: the extension to A_2 ∖ {−1/3} (equivalently, from 2A+1 to (2A_2+1) ∖ {−1/3}), proved and left unmarked. Alternatives the author might prefer: restrict to the orbits avoiding −1/3 (the RepDomain of theo:rep), or state the proposition only for rings with 3 ∉ A^× (but A_2 = Z_2 always has 3 a unit, so the extension clause needs the puncture regardless).

What is 'the 2-completion of A' (l.52)? Reading taken: the uniform completion for the 2-adic uniformity (the uniformity of the absolute value |x| = 2^{-ν_2(x)}), for any uniform ring structure on A whose topology is 2-adic. Z_2 through ι is used as a concrete model, justified by Syracuse.completion_ringEquiv. The algebraic completion lim A/2^nA is not formalized here. For these rings it is also Z_2 (A/2^nA ≅ Z/2^nZ is proved), but that identification is not formalized.

OQ-42 (b): 2 ≠ 0 is assumed wherever A_2 or ι enters. For A = Z/2Z, l.52 is false (Finding 3) and halves are not unique, so nothing is claimed about its extension. Is Z/2Z meant to be excluded from 'Z/2Z-ring'?
OQ-42 (a): the l.52 claim needs integrality (ZMod 4). Is 'integral' (l.50) part of the definition of a Z/2Z-ring (l.52)? Reading taken: yes (IsZ2Ring).

kb_proposals: The map A → ℤ₂ of a ℤ/2ℤ-ring with 2 ≠ 0 is Syracuse.toZ2 = PadicInt.lift of zmodPow. Here A/2ⁿA ≃ ℤ/2ⁿℤ comes from CharP plus 'every x is an integer mod 2ⁿ' (exists_int_two_pow_dvd_sub). A ring hom A → ZMod 2ⁿ is unique (ringHom_zmodPow_ext), which gives the compatibility, toZ2_unique and naturality for free. Statements transfer along any ring hom by f_map and T_map (T-syr-completion).

The 2-adic topology: state with [TopologicalSpace A] (hA : IsAdic (Ideal.span {2})). hasBasis_nhds_two gives the balls {y | 2ⁿ ∣ y − x}, and continuousAt_iff_two gives the ε–δ form. ℤ_[2] satisfies it (isAdic_padicInt). WithIdeal ⟨span {2}⟩ is the canonical instance (isAdic_withIdeal: unfold IsAdic; rfl). Never put WithIdeal on ℤ or ℤ_[2], which carry global topologies. ZMod n carries one (discrete) only through Mathlib.Topology.Instances.ZMod, which Completion.lean does not import (T-syr-completion).

UniformSpace.Completion A ≃+* ℤ_[2] is RingEquiv.ofBijective (Completion.extensionHom ι hc) (Completion.cPkg.compareEquiv pkg).bijective. The two functions are defeq (both are cPkg.extend ι). Annotate the result of compareEquiv as `Completion A ≃ᵤ ℤ_[2]`, or the AbstractCompletion local instances are not found. Ring endomorphisms of ℤ₂ are trivial (toZ2_unique at A = ℤ_[2]), so any two ring isos onto ℤ₂ agree (ringEquiv_padicInt_unique) (T-syr-completion).

T has no limit at −1/3. The integer sequences (4^{j+1}−1)/3 → −1/3 with T = 1, and (10·4^{j+1}−1)/3 → −1/3 with T = 5 (Syracuse.not_continuousWithinAt_extension_T, for any Hausdorff 2-adic target B and ring hom A → B). Cast integer identities into a ring that may have positive characteristic with congrArg Int.cast plus push_cast, not exact_mod_cast (T-syr-completion).
